_comment: One card, one skill, one artifact. This is the loose board for applying a single stelow stage skill to something that already exists, and it exists because the 18-stage chain is the wrong shape for a question.

menu.when: a part of a codebase needs judging before anyone builds on it
a plan or proposal exists and needs to be attacked before it is spent
a diff or branch needs reviewing as work, not as style
a screen or flow needs to be read the way a user would
two existing architecture choices need comparing on evidence
the shape of a system is still open and options need naming
two existing interface options need comparing on evidence
an interface is still open and must not be guessed
a shaped pitch is needed: appetite, boundary, rabbit holes
an approved design needs a technical plan someone can execute
one scoped slice should be executed end to end, without the chain
AI-written code needs a test plan that catches real defects
tests exist or were just written and need to be run, not assumed
new code needs to be held against this project's standards

columns.label: Open
columns.instructions: A card arrives here and nothing runs. Make it answerable before it moves: what is being judged, where it lives (repo, branch, diff, document), and what artifact the requester wants back. If the request names a skill, keep the name. If it names more than one, split it into more cards now: this board runs one skill per card, and a card carrying three questions has no artifact anyone can review.

columns.label: Run
columns.instructions:
Load exactly one skill from the menu and run it on what the card names. Say in one line which skill you picked and why it beats the neighbours in the menu, then do the work and attach the artifact the skill produces, under its own name.

If the card needs a second skill to answer, stop: park it, say in one line which cards it should become, and let a person split it. Two skills in one run produce two half-artifacts and no one can review either.

Read what the card names before reading anything else; do not widen the scope to the whole repository, and do not fix anything you were not asked to judge.

columns.label: Review
columns.instructions:
Read the artifact and answer one question: does it settle what the card asked? Approve it and the card closes. Send it back if the artifact answers a different question, cites nothing, or leaves the judgement to the reader; say which of those three in one line, because a send-back with no reason is a second round nobody learns from.

This column is a person's. While the card waits here it carries `needs-human` and one nudge, so a waiting card cannot be mistaken for a dead run.
